ev.q: CDC analyzed 2016 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data.
The prevalences of disability overall and by disability type, and access to health care by disability type, were estimated.
One in four noninstitutionalized U.S. adults (25.7%, representing an estimated 61.4 million persons) reported any disability
one in four (61 million) U.S. adults reported any disability
Among all age groups, the prevalences of any disability and of each type were higher among women than among men
All analyses were stratified by age group (18–44, 45–64, and ≥65 years).
BRFSS data are cross-sectional, and causality among sociodemographic characteristics, health care access, and disability cannot be inferred.
BRFSS is an ongoing state-based, random-digit–dialed telephone survey of noninstitutionalized U.S. adults

methods_quotes.q: Prevalences (with 95% confidence intervals) were calculated for any disability and disability type by sex, race/ethnicity
Persons who responded “yes” to at least one disability question were identified as having any disability.
Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design.
Estimate not available because relative standard error >0.30.
